children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Thursday.
WHEAT - Down 3 to 5 cents per bushel
CBOT wheat futures
dropped for a third straight session on Thursday, pressured by a rise in the US dollar and as traders monitor prospects for diplomatic efforts to ease Black Sea export disruptions.
Strength in the US dollar can make US exports more expensive for overseas buyers.

The US Department of Agriculture said net US wheat export sales in the week ended September 17 totaled 267,600 metric tons for shipment in the current marketing year. A Reuters poll of traders estimated between 350,000 and 600,000 tons.

The governor of Russia's southern Krasnodar region, a major agricultural producer, has declared a state of emergency over Ukrainian drone attacks that have inhibited the export of grain, a move which allows those affected to receive compensation.
Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up attacks on the other side's grain vessels in the Black Sea in recent months, sending global prices higher.

Only eight countries bought wheat from Russia, the world's biggest wheat exporter, in September, down from 26 a year earlier, data from the Russian Grain Union lobby group showed on Wednesday. The number of buyers in August fell to 16 from 43 in the same month last year.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was 4-1/2 cents lower at $7.04 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was down 5-1/2 cents to $7.66-1/4 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last down 3 cents at $7.25-3/4 a bushel.
CORN - Mixed, down 2 cents to up 2 cents
CBOT corn futures
were mixed as investors waited to see if Thursday's US-China summit yields progress in agricultural trade.
The US Department of Agriculture said net US corn export sales in the week ended September 17 totaled 838,300 metric tons for shipment in the current marketing year, below trade expectations.
Strength in the dollar index
was also pressuring US grains by making them more expensive for overseas buyers.

Ukraine has asked the European Union to increase its quota for bioethanol exports this year by 60,000 metric tons, Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi said on Thursday, after a doubling in domestic production capacity.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last 1-1/2 cents lower at $5.27-1/2 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Up 2 to 4 cents per bushel
CBOT soybean futures
firmed ahead of the closely watched US-China summit.
The US Department of Agriculture said net US soybean export sales in the week ended September 17 totaled 582,400 metric tons for shipment in the current marketing year, below trade expectations.
Separately, USDA on Thursday said that private exporters reported sales of 120,000 metric tons of soybeans for delivery to China during the 2026/2027 marketing year.

Weather forecasters are calling for a widespread storm system to reach the US Plains and the western two-thirds of the Midwest, bringing heavy rain through the weekend and potentially adding additional delays to this fall's corn and soybean harvest.
A second wet weather system early next week is also expected to impact the Midwest, causing further harvest headaches for farmers and soy processors needing new-crop supplies for crushing.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last up 3-3/4 cents at $13.21-3/4 per bushel.
